- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the low-end of the range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to overestimate short-term volatility in early 30-day forecasts; apply a 3–5% downward bias to the first 5–7 days.  
- After a strong price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 2–4% downward correction.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 1–3% downward bias toward the end of the forecast horizon.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, model tends to underestimate the dip; add 2–5% upward bias to the early part of the forecast.
